categories.main_business_segments: Restaurant Brands International (RBI) operates four primary business segments, each corresponding to a major quick service restaurant brand: Tim Hortons (TH), Burger King (BK), Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen (PLK), and Firehouse Subs (FHS). Each brand is managed independently and represents a distinct operating and reportable segment. The company’s revenues are generated from supply chain sales, franchise and property revenues, and advertising and other services across these segments.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: RBI’s core operations rely on a franchise business model supported by proprietary restaurant operating procedures, supply chain management, and digital technologies. Tim Hortons operates its own coffee roasting and fondant manufacturing facilities, while other brands source products from approved third-party suppliers. The company invests in proprietary point-of-sale (rPOS) systems, digital ordering platforms, loyalty programs, and drive-thru modernization, and maintains strict supplier approval and food safety standards.
categories.primary_customers_markets: RBI primarily serves individual consumers through its global network of franchised quick service restaurants. Its key customer base includes coffee and baked goods consumers (Tim Hortons), fast food hamburger customers (Burger King), fried chicken and seafood consumers (Popeyes), and sub sandwich customers (Firehouse Subs). The company’s end markets span breakfast, lunch, dinner, and snack dayparts, with a focus on convenience, value, and speed.
categories.geographic_coverage: RBI operates in over 100 countries, with a significant presence in North America (Canada and the United States), as well as substantial operations in Europe, Asia, Latin America, and other international markets. Tim Hortons is the largest in Canada, Burger King has a broad international footprint, Popeyes is expanding globally, and Firehouse Subs is primarily in North America but targeted for international growth.
categories.supply_chain_position: RBI primarily operates downstream in the supply chain as a franchisor and brand owner, focusing on restaurant operations, marketing, and customer engagement. For Tim Hortons, it also acts as a vertically integrated supplier, manufacturing and distributing key products to franchisees. For other brands, it approves suppliers and manages purchasing cooperatives but does not directly manufacture most products.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: RBI’s strategic priorities include accelerating net restaurant growth, enhancing guest experience, increasing restaurant sales and profitability, strengthening drive-thru and delivery channels, and leveraging digital and technology initiatives such as loyalty programs and mobile ordering. The company emphasizes product innovation, operational excellence, and sustainability, with ongoing investments in digital modernization and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) initiatives.
categories.revenue_model: RBI generates revenue through four main streams: (1) supply chain sales to franchisees and retailers (primarily for Tim Hortons), (2) franchise revenues from royalties and franchise fees based on a percentage of franchise restaurant sales, (3) property revenues from leasing or subleasing properties to franchisees, and (4) advertising revenues and other services funded by franchisee contributions. Nearly all restaurants are franchised, making royalty and fee income the dominant revenue source.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: RBI competes with major global and regional quick service restaurant chains such as McDonald’s, Wendy’s, KFC, Subway, Starbucks, and other fast food and fast casual brands, as well as independent local operators and new entrants like virtual brands and delivery-only kitchens. RBI is one of the world’s largest QSR companies by system-wide sales and restaurant count, with strong brand recognition and global scale.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2022, RBI reported over $39.7 billion in annual system-wide sales and operated approximately 30,700 restaurants worldwide. The company achieved consolidated system-wide sales growth of 13.4% in 2022, with net income of $1.48 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $2.38 billion. RBI has demonstrated consistent growth in restaurant count and sales, with a highly franchised, asset-light model and significant international expansion.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: RBI’s value proposition centers on iconic, globally recognized brands offering affordable, high-quality, and convenient food and beverage options. The company differentiates itself through its scale, franchise expertise, digital innovation, and ability to leverage best practices across brands. RBI emphasizes menu innovation, operational efficiency, and a strong focus on guest experience, while supporting franchisee profitability and community engagement.
